comparisons.evidence: P's "Corporate congestion liability (S5)" and Q's "Trip-Generator Reliability Regime" both target high-leverage institutional traffic generation. P's focus on freight chokepoints ("S8") and Q's focus on building-level consolidation ("Building Logistics Kernel") target similarly impactful bottlenecks.

P provides a highly credible, decentralized causal path via an app-based "decaying pheromone traffic broadcast (S2)". Q offers an equally sound network-based mechanism using multi-party matching math to shorten trips in its "Entitlement-Preserving Seat Exchange".

P establishes real-world viability by anchoring its freight strategy ("S8") in data from an existing NYC pilot. Q addresses behavioral and political barriers directly by ensuring its matching framework "preserves service entitlement" so users do not resist location swaps.

Both provide exceptionally crisp, low-cost prototyping steps. P describes clear data-buying and simulation protocols, while Q outlines precise field tests involving a human dispatcher at a single building or running offline matches on anonymized records.

While P creatively borrows from ant foraging models, Q provides a brilliant and deeply non-obvious reframing by adapting kidney-exchange algorithms ("Entitlement-Preserving Seat Exchange") to resolve systemic school and clinic commute patterns without forcing users to give up their rights.

P's mechanisms cover routing, zoning, and liability levers. Q achieves a broader reach across distinct regions of the solution space by systematically translating distributed computer systems architecture (caching, batching, deduplication) into physical transit solutions.

Q demonstrates superior curation of the reader's attention by including a dedicated "Merge by causal mechanism" matrix that transparently groups and distills 21 granular ideas into 11 strictly distinct causal pathways, whereas P relies on a more informal pruning process.
